--- Page 1 (Beckerman_36a) --- 13 JULY 1945 MANILA DEAR MOM AND DAD: AM ENCLOSING SOME PHOTOS THAT I TOOK IN NEW GUINEA ON THE WAY UP. ALSO A FEW TAKEN HERE. ABE AND I SPENT SUNDAY AFTERNOON TOGETHER. WE SNAPPEP A ROLL OF FILMS ON MY CAMERA; BUT VERY UNFORT- UNATELY THEY DID NOT COME OUT WELL AT ALL. I THINK MY CAMERA IS COMPLETELY BROKEN AND AM NOT GOING TO RISK ANY MORE FILM ON IT. AM GOING TO FAk BORROW ANOTHER CAMERA THIS COMING SUNDAY AND TRY MY LUCK AGAIN WITH ABE. HOPE THEY WILL COME OUT BETTER THE NEXT TIME. I WILL SEND YOU THE ROLL WITH NEXT LETTER. OF OUR BAD PICTURES THE NEXT TIME. AT LEAST YOU WILL BE ABLE TO SEE US AS WE ARE AS NURE OF LAST ETH EVER IG H UTH'S LONG TOER. RYTH. IN RECERIS GA V MAIL LETTER. I GUESS THE HOUSE IS PRETTY DESERTED BY NOW. HOPE EVERYTHING IS ALL RIGHT AT HOME. HAVE YOU RECEIVED --- Page 2 (Beckerman_36b) --- THE CHECK YET THAT I WROTE YOU ABOUT? PRICES HERE ARE SKY HIGH. BUT LUCKILY THE ARMY SUPPLIES ALL OUR NEEDS AND THERE IS NO NEED OF GOING TO CIVILIAN STORES. I'M SNEAKING THIS OFF TO YOU DURING WORKING HOURS SO WILL HAVE TO COME TO A CLOSE. LOVE AND REGARDS TO ALL. WILL WRITE AGAIN SOON AND AM WAITING FOR MOM'S LETTERS TO START ARRIVING. JACK.
Archivist notes
The letter is written in a casual, personal style, indicating a close relationship between the sender and the recipients. The sender is also inquiring about a check, suggesting financial matters are a concern.
